A.8 A Reproducible Solver and Certified Numerical Error

For n≥1n\geq 1, the following solver minimizes the constrained objective (8). Inputs are the retained matrix XX, clipped response vector y∈[0,1]ny\in[0,1]^{n}, RR, and the channel-specific ρn\rho_{n}. There is no unpenalized intercept and no automatic centering, feature standardization, or response rescaling. A constant feature, when used, is part of xx and subject to both the penalty and norm bound. Any deliberate preprocessing must first be reflected in RR, noise bounds, and design calibration.

Let g⁡(θ)=‖y−X​θ‖22/(2​n)g(\theta)=\|y-X\theta\|_{2}^{2}/(2n) and F⁡(θ)=g⁡(θ)+ρn​‖θ‖1F(\theta)=g(\theta)+\rho_{n}\|\theta\|_{1}. Its gradient is 1-Lipschitz because ‖X⊤​X/n‖op≤1\|X^{\top}X/n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq 1. Start at θ(0)=0\theta^{(0)}=0 and use step size one. For iteration jj set

v=θ(j)−∇g​(θ(j)),z=sign⁡(v)​(|v|−ρn)+,θ(j+1)=z​min⁡{1,R/‖z‖2},v=\theta^{(j)}-\nabla g(\theta^{(j)}),\qquad z=\operatorname{sign}(v)(|v|-\rho_{n})_{+},\qquad\theta^{(j+1)}=z\min\{1,R/\|z\|_{2}\}, (60)

with the last expression interpreted as zero when z=0z=0. The soft threshold and scaling together are the proximal map of ρn∥⋅∥1+ι{∥⋅∥2≤R}\rho_{n}\|\cdot\|_{1}+\iota_{\{\|\cdot\|_{2}\leq R\}}, where the last term is the convex indicator (zero on the ball, +∞+\infty outside). To check this, set a=(‖z‖2/R−1)+a=(\|z\|_{2}/R-1)_{+}, and choose wj=sign⁡(zj)w_{j}=\operatorname{sign}(z_{j}) if zj≠0z_{j}\neq 0, and wj=vj/ρnw_{j}=v_{j}/\rho_{n} otherwise. Then w∈∂‖θ(j+1)‖1w\in\partial\|\theta^{(j+1)}\|_{1}, v−θ(j+1)=ρn​w+a​θ(j+1)v-\theta^{(j+1)}=\rho_{n}w+a\theta^{(j+1)}, and a⁡(‖θ(j+1)‖2−R)=0a(\|\theta^{(j+1)}\|_{2}-R)=0, which are sufficient convex optimality conditions for the proximal problem.

At the new iterate form vF=∇g​(θ(j+1))+ρn​wv_{F}=\nabla g(\theta^{(j+1)})+\rho_{n}w and the computable certificate

Gj=⟨vF,θ(j+1)⟩+R​‖vF‖2≥F⁡(θ(j+1))−min‖θ‖2≤R⁡F⁡(θ)≥0.G_{j}=\langle v_{F},\theta^{(j+1)}\rangle+R\|v_{F}\|_{2}\geq F(\theta^{(j+1)})-\min_{\|\theta\|_{2}\leq R}F(\theta)\geq 0. (61)

The first inequality follows by minimizing the supporting affine minorant of FF over the ball. Stop at the first certified Gj≤εopt,n:=s​ρn2/(8​κ)G_{j}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt},n}:=s\rho_{n}^{2}/(8\kappa). This is a deterministic selection convention for approximate fits; it need not return the minimum-norm exact minimizer. The latter convention is well defined because the minimizer set is nonempty, compact, and convex and the squared Euclidean norm is strictly convex. Measurability of the exact convention follows, for example, by taking limits of the unique minimizers of F⁡(θ)+ϵ​‖θ‖22F(\theta)+\epsilon\|\theta\|_{2}^{2} on the ball as ϵ↓0\epsilon\downarrow 0. The finite algorithm uses measurable arithmetic and a first-passage stopping rule.

Proposition A.10 (Solver termination and precision accounting)

In exact arithmetic the stopping rule above terminates. A sufficient upper bound on the iterations is 1+⌈16​R2/εopt,n2⌉1+\lceil 16R^{2}/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt},n}^{2}\rceil. Each iteration costs O⁡(n​d)O(nd) arithmetic operations. The returned fit satisfies Proposition 3.1, including its numerical-error contribution.

Proof A.11

Proximal descent and the 1-Lipschitz gradient give F⁡(θ(j))−F⁡(θ(j+1))≥12​‖θ(j+1)−θ(j)‖22F(\theta^{(j)})-F(\theta^{(j+1)})\geq\frac{1}{2}\|\theta^{(j+1)}-\theta^{(j)}\|_{2}^{2}. Since F⁡(0)≤1/2F(0)\leq 1/2 and F≥0F\geq 0, the sum of these squared steps is at most one. The proximal optimality equation implies

‖vF+a​θ(j+1)‖2≤‖θ(j)−θ(j+1)‖2+‖∇g​(θ(j+1))−∇g​(θ(j))‖2≤2​‖θ(j+1)−θ(j)‖2.\|v_{F}+a\theta^{(j+1)}\|_{2}\leq\|\theta^{(j)}-\theta^{(j+1)}\|_{2}+\|\nabla g(\theta^{(j+1)})-\nabla g(\theta^{(j)})\|_{2}\leq 2\|\theta^{(j+1)}-\theta^{(j)}\|_{2}.

Using complementarity and ‖θ(j+1)‖2≤R\|\theta^{(j+1)}\|_{2}\leq R in (61) gives Gj≤4​R​‖θ(j+1)−θ(j)‖2G_{j}\leq 4R\|\theta^{(j+1)}-\theta^{(j)}\|_{2}. If all of the first JJ certificates exceeded εopt,n\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt},n}, the squared-step sum would exceed J​εopt,n2/(16​R2)J\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt},n}^{2}/(16R^{2}). This is impossible for the stated JJ. The certificate implies the objective-gap condition in Lemma A.5.

The iteration bound is conservative; it establishes certified termination rather than practical speed. For floating-point implementation, verify feasibility and evaluate an upper bound on (61) using directed rounding or explicitly bounded arithmetic residuals. An approximately valid subgradient with a certified Euclidean discrepancy ee adds at most 2​R​e2Re to the certificate. Accept an iterate only when a certified upper bound on its Euclidean norm is at most RR. A fixed iteration limit or small successive-step difference without these error bounds is not the certificate used in our guarantee. If the tolerance is not met, use trivial radii until a certified fit is available; the concrete rates assume the stated certificate is obtained.

For a different certified objective gap εopt,a,t\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt},a,t}, the general additional prediction term is

Ea,t=2​(εopt,a,t+4​ωn​εopt,a,t2/ρn2)/κ.E_{a,t}=2\sqrt{\bigl(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt},a,t}+4\omega_{n}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt},a,t}^{2}/\rho_{n}^{2}\bigr)/\kappa}.

Apply this separately by channel and add twice the recommendation-weighted sum of Er+Z​maxi​EibE^{r}+Z\max_{i}E_{i}^{b} to the cumulative width interface. Under the prescribed tolerance these sums are already included in the coefficient 77 and hence in AA; there is no omitted fixed numerical error accumulated over TT rounds.

Full online cost and calibration. For a fixed channel, all corruption candidates use the same X,y,ρnX,y,\rho_{n} and solver stopping criterion. Only an action receiving a newly retained observation requires a new fit; cached fits for other actions retain their certified objective gaps for the unchanged objectives, since ρn\rho_{n} depends on nn, not calendar time. There are at most (m+1)​T(m+1)T changed fits. A conservative total arithmetic cost is

O⁡((m+1)​d​∑a=1K∑n=1Naest​(T+1)n⁡[1+R2εopt,n2]+T⁡{K⁡(m+1)​d+K​|𝒢|+m}),O\left((m+1)d\sum_{a=1}^{K}\sum_{n=1}^{N_{a}^{\mathrm{est}}(T+1)}n\left[1+\frac{R^{2}}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt},n}^{2}}\right]+T\{K(m+1)d+K|\mathcal{G}|+m\}\right),

using the largest channel-specific iteration bound in the first term. Computing all fitted scores costs O⁡(K⁡(m+1)​d)O(K(m+1)d) per round; scoring the grid costs O⁡(K​|𝒢|)O(K|\mathcal{G}|), and the master and price updates add O⁡(|𝒢|+K+m)O(|\mathcal{G}|+K+m). Storing retained raw samples costs O⁡(T⁡(d+m))O(T(d+m)). No delayed refitting or unanalysed stale estimator is used. In FE, κx,Lx\kappa_{x},L_{x} and the model bounds are supplied and (49) is computed directly. In OP, the supplied pair must be justified for the actual trajectory by Condition 3.2; the method does not compute the smallest RE constant. Without justified bounds, trivial radii remain valid but these informative-width rates do not follow.

1+v+z−1+v=z1+v+z+1+v,\sqrt{1+v+z}-\sqrt{1+v}=\frac{z}{\sqrt{1+v+z}+\sqrt{1+v}},

whose denominator is at most 4​v∨14\sqrt{v\vee 1}. Telescoping gives at most 4​(1+S−1)≤4​S4(\sqrt{1+S}-1)\leq 4\sqrt{S}. Let 0<ϵ≤1/20<\epsilon\leq 1/2 be constant. On an event of failure at most δcov/2\delta_{\mathrm{cov}}/2, every active round with ϵ⁡(t−1)≥8​K​ℓ\epsilon(t-1)\geq 8K\ell satisfies

ℛest0≤C⁡[h​K​(n0+ℓ)ϵ+AFE​K​Tϵ],ψest​(Γ)≤C​K​Γ​HTκFE​ϵ.\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{est}}^{0}\leq C\left[\frac{hK(n_{0}+\ell)}{\epsilon}+A_{\mathrm{FE}}\sqrt{\frac{KT}{\epsilon}}\right],\qquad\psi_{\mathrm{est}}(\Gamma)\leq\frac{CK\Gamma H_{T}}{\kappa_{\mathrm{FE}}\epsilon}. (65)

Proof A.15

Generate the independent forced coins and uniform draws for all calendar times, including unused draws after stopping. Before this time charge at most 2​h2h per active round. If the threshold exceeds TT, the displayed burn-in term already bounds the whole horizon. For shared FE use elapsed post-initialization time in the count argument. Initialization samples can only increase that count, and Lemma A.8 applies to the combined retained prefix; no comparison of two different fitted estimators is used.

A.10 Failure Probabilities and Concrete Substitution

For known FE combine the coordinate-noise event, the forced-design event, and the forced-count event; their failure is at most δest+δcov\delta_{\mathrm{est}}+\delta_{\mathrm{cov}}. For known OP combine noise with Condition 3.2. For shared OP add the candidate event. None of these events is obtained by conditioning the clean martingale increments on successful estimation. Instead, bound the score gap pathwise on the good event and by hh on its complement. This produces the explicit h​δtot​Th\delta_{\mathrm{tot}}T expected-regret contribution. Mean-zero clean-feedback terms are removed using the original filtration before this event split, as in Appendix B.

Equations (65), (67), and (68) provide every input to the modular allocation theorems. They include the chosen solver’s numerical error through AA, retain the actual curvature and tolerance dependence, and have no corruption-dependent burn-in. If κ\kappa is small or the calibrated threshold exceeds available data, the bound can be larger than TT; the unconditional range bound Reg⁡(T)≤T\Reg(T)\leq T still applies. Neither convexity nor an unsuccessful calibration implies sublinear regret.

For the null action, set β𝚗𝚞𝚕𝚕,tZ,Γ=0\beta_{\mathtt{null},t}^{Z,\Gamma}=0, F^𝚗𝚞𝚕𝚕,t​(λ)=0\widehat{F}_{\mathtt{null},t}(\lambda)=0, and F0​(𝚗𝚞𝚕𝚕,x,λ)=0F^{0}(\mathtt{null},x;\lambda)=0.

Appendix C Proof of the Unknown-Corruption Guarantee

The proof compares recommendations computed from one common realized estimator history. It does not compare counterfactual histories that different candidates would have generated. Direct corruption enters twice when transferring the master comparison to clean scores, and once in the resource conversion. The cumulative confidence term is separate.

C.1 One Common Confidence and Width Event

Lemma C.1 (Shared estimates and all valid grid points)

For the concrete module of Appendices A.2–A.3, under the FE calibration or the OP trajectory condition, one event of failure at most δest+δcov\delta_{\mathrm{est}}+\delta_{\mathrm{cov}} gives pointwise confidence for every valid Γ∈𝒢\Gamma\in\mathcal{G}. On this event the FE grid-uniform width interface holds with (65). For OP, intersect also with Condition 5.3’s event; then (68) supplies that interface, with total failure at most δest+δcov+δcand\delta_{\mathrm{est}}+\delta_{\mathrm{cov}}+\delta_{\mathrm{cand}}.

Proof C.2

The estimator sample set (27) is exactly the initialization-augmented FE or all-realized OP set in (45). Lemma A.3 covers its obtained prefixes, including stopping. In FE, Lemma A.8 applies directly to the combined initialization and later forced samples, and Lemma A.14 supplies the count event. In OP, the retained design is precisely the design in Condition 3.2. For every response channel, the data, ρn\rho_{n}, and certified objective-gap tolerance are common to all candidates. Lemma A.5 is deterministic for any corruption vector on the noise event. Therefore Lemma A.1 covers all valid candidates simultaneously, without a candidate-dependent noise theorem or a candidate-dependent fit. The FE width bound holds for arbitrary recommendations. The OP width bound uses Proposition A.18 and the additional candidate event. Since CZ≤T⁡(1+Z)C_{Z}\leq T(1+Z), the grid contains a valid point and the same event permits the post hoc substitution of Γ⋆\Gamma^{\star}.

Thus, on the appropriate common event,

2​∑t=tinit+1TIt​βa^tΓ⋆,tZ,Γ⋆≤ℛsh0+ψest​(Γ⋆).2\sum_{t=t_{\mathrm{init}}+1}^{T}I_{t}\beta_{\widehat{a}_{t}^{\Gamma^{\star}},t}^{Z,\Gamma^{\star}}\leq\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{sh}}^{0}+\psi_{\mathrm{est}}(\Gamma^{\star}). (85)

Initialization is charged separately, so ℛsh0\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{sh}}^{0} is a post-initialization width bound. The parameters of the OP event concern the algorithm’s actual shared trajectory, not the trajectory of a candidate run alone.
